summary: Robert P. Goldman is an Indologist who studied at Columbia University (~1960–1964) and the University of Pennsylvania (~1964–1971), also learning from Shivaram Dattatray Joshi, T. S. Srinivasa Sastri, and T. Shrinivas Shastri. He held a post at UC Berkeley (~1971).

Robert S. Nelson is a historian and archaeologist who studied at Rice University (~1965–1969) and New York University (~1969–1978). He served as a professor at the University of Chicago (~1977–2005) and held a post at Yale University (~2005–2021).
Robert Warren Clark is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under doctoral supervisor Karen C. Lang (attested 1994) as well as adviser and teacher K. L. Seshagiri Rao.
Robert Zimmermann (1874–1931) was an Indologist who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1907–1913). He held an academic post at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai, from around 1914 to 1930.

Robin Coningham is a scholar of archaeology and Indology who studied at King's College (1985–1994) and the University of Cambridge (~1989–1994). He held posts at the University of Bradford (~1994–2005) and Durham University (2005).

Roderick Chisholm (1916–1999) was a philosopher who studied at Harvard University (~1938–1942). He held long-term posts at Brown University (~1947–1987) and the University of Massachusetts Amherst (~1987–1996).

Roderick S. Bucknell is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. He held academic posts at the University of Queensland from around 1976 to 1998 and as Associate Professor from around 1999 to 2002.

Roderick Whitfield is a scholar of archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the British Museum (attested 1986) and SOAS University of London, where he was an emeritus professor (attested 2011).

Roger R. Jackson is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He studied at Wesleyan University and UW–Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, among others, and held an Associate Professor post at Carleton College (~1989–2016).

Roger T. Ames is a philosopher and sinologist who studied at the University of British Columbia and National Taiwan University. He was a professor at the University of Hawaii (~1978–2016) and later held a post at Peking University (~2016).
Roland Steiner is a scholar of Indology and Tibetology. He studied under Michael Hahn (attested 1990) and held an assistant professor post at the University of Marburg (attested 2002).

Roland Wenzlhuemer is a historian who studied at the University of Salzburg (~1996–2002). He held academic posts at Heidelberg University (~2008–2017) and Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~2017).

Rolf Alfred Stein was a scholar in Tibetology and Sinology who studied in Berlin and Paris under Chavannes, Pelliot, Maspero, Demiéville, and Bacot. He held posts at INALCO (~1948–1951), EPHE (~1951–1975), and Collège de France (1965–1981).

Rolf Scheuermann is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Vienna (attested 2010) under MA supervisor Helmut Tauscher, and also studied under traditional teacher Khenpo Chodrak Tenphel.

Romila Thapar is a historian and Indologist who studied at Panjab University and the University of London under A. L. Basham. She held posts at the University of Delhi (~1963–1970) and Jawaharlal Nehru University (attested 2001).
Ron Garry is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teacher Lama Tharchin Rinpoche and teacher Tulku Thubten Rinpoche.
Ron Leifer was a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied under Agehananda Bharati (1964) and traditional teacher Khenpo Karthar Rinpoche.

Ronald D. Schwartz is a scholar in Tibetology and sociology. In 1998, he was attested as Professor of Sociology at Memorial University of Newfoundland and as an Honorary Research Fellow at the University of Hong Kong.

Ronald E. Purser works in religious studies, philosophy, and management, and studied under Koshin Ogui (1985). He held posts at Loyola University Chicago (~1989–1995) and San Francisco State University (~1995).

Ronald Egan is a Sinologist who earned his Ph.D. at Harvard (~1971–1977). He held posts at Harvard (~1977–1986), Wellesley College (~1986–1993), UC Santa Barbara (~1993–2012), and Stanford University (~2012).
